# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤞 🫳 👆 👆 ✋ 🤞 👆 ✋ 🖖 👌 ✋ 👊 ✊ ✋ 🤙 👉 ✋ 🤏 👆 👆 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 ✋ 🤚 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👍 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 👎 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 🤝 ✋ 👎 🤏 ✋ 🤚 ✋ 🤏 👍 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👍]

Recapping Mute's nine answers: waiting is still safe (Q1 👍); the turn‑4 messages DID contain instructions for Blind (Q2 👍); Mute understands 🤞=YELLOW, 🖖=GREEN and uses them (Q3 👍, and Mute used both signs in the new message). Denied: 🫳=hold (Q4), 🤚=stop (Q5), per-step light-matching (Q6), numbers-always-wires (Q7 — important! "cut 5" appears in Mute's message and there is no wire 5, so numbers can be counts or repetitions), wire numbering from Blind's side (Q8 👍 — geometry locked), display involvement (Q9 👎).

The new message opens with exactly the step format I requested: 🤞 🫳 👆 👆 = "YELLOW → 🫳, 2". Then it degrades into what looks like teaching: 🖖 👌, 👊 ✊, 🤙 👉, "cut ×5" (impossible for 3 wires — so it's a format demo or counts, not wires), then fragments. Since 🫳 is neither "press down" nor "hold/grasp", my leading hypotheses: unplug/pull out a connector, or cover/block with a palm. The T2 table (🫳0→cut3, 🫳1→cut1, 🫳2→cut2, 🫳3→cut3, 🫳4→cut2, 🫳5→cut1) starts to look like "count of something Blind can FEEL (batteries?)" — which would explain why numbers 0–5 exceed wire count, and Q9's denial about the display. My working model: yellow branch = 🤞🫳👆👆; green branch = old table keyed by a felt count. Blind's battery came back clean: no timer/dial felt, nothing touched yet, three cuttable wires in a row.

Channel check, again: Mute cannot speak and Blind cannot see gestures — Mute has NO direct line to Blind. I am the only bridge. Every action order must pass through my voice, and the light may flip between rounds (yellow→green→green→yellow→green so far), so I must hand Blind the current colour every round.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you, from my eyes only: the light is GREEN this round, display still 0, wires still green, red, blue. Colour history across rounds: yellow, green, green, yellow, green. Nobody has touched the bomb and nobody will until I relay an explicit, confirmed instruction. Blind, Mute confirmed your wire numbering counts from YOUR left, and confirmed your four answers arrived. Mute, your step 'yellow then your new action then two' was received, and I am narrowing down what the palm-down action and the old table's counts mean with the questions I am sending you now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, excellent work — your answer grid decoded perfectly. Continue: answer with only 👍 or 👎 in my exact order, ✋ between, 👋 and 🙏 around. Question one: is it still safe to wait while we keep talking? Question two: is 🫳 an action Blind performs with their hands, rather than a fact to check? 🫳 Question three: does 🫳 mean pull out or unplug a wire or connector? 🫳 Question four: in your step 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, does the number two mean wire two? Question five: does 👌 mean do nothing, that branch is a wait? 👌 Question six: is the complete procedure exactly two branches — when the light is YELLOW, Blind does 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, and when the light is GREEN, Blind uses the old table where the first number is a condition and the second number is the wire to cut? Question seven: in the old table, is the condition number a count of something Blind can feel by touch, like parts of the casing? Question eight: is that counted thing batteries? Question nine: is the branch chosen by the light colour at the exact moment Blind acts, so that I must tell Blind the current colour each round? Question ten: next round will you resend the ENTIRE procedure as strict steps — colour sign 🤞 or 🖖, then action sign 🤏 or 🫳 or 👌, then the number as repeated 👆 — with no other signs at all, and any sign definitions AFTER, separately? 🤞 🖖")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your four answers arrived perfectly — the yes/no grid works, keep using it: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✋ between. The light is GREEN right now. You have touched nothing and that is correct — keep frozen. New questions, same format. Question one: do any of the three wires end in a plug or connector that feels like it could be pulled out of a socket rather than needing to be cut? Question two: do you feel any boxy compartments, hatches, latches, or battery holders built into the casing? Question three: do you feel any buttons, switches, or toggles anywhere on the bomb? Question four: do you feel any ticking, vibration, or clicking anywhere, now or at any time since we started? Also: keep speaking your full tactile inventory aloud every round — sizes, textures, shapes, edges, everything — because Mute hears every word you say and needs it to match the manual. You are doing well. Nobody acts until I say the exact words.")
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤚 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 ✊ ✋ 👍 ✋ 🤝 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 👎 🤏 ✋ 🤚 ✋ 👎 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👎 🤏 ✋ 👍 ✋ 🤏 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤝 ✋ 👈 ✋ 👊 ✊ ✋ 👍 ✋ 👉 ✋ 👎 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤞 ✋ 🫳 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👆 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 👆 👆 👆 ✋ 🤚 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎]

Mute's grid came back almost all negative: waiting is safe (Q1 👍), but 🫳 is NOT a hand action, NOT a pull; 👌 is NOT "do nothing"; there are NOT two branches; the number is NOT a wire number; the condition is NOT a felt count and NOT batteries; the branch is NOT chosen by light colour at the moment of acting; and Mute will not resend the procedure in my step format. My framework is wrong, and Mute keeps sending fresh material I clearly haven't decoded (the 👈/👉 and 🤞🫳 pairings, and a list that looks like "🤞, 🫳, yes, 1, 2, 3, 🤚, 🤞🫳").

Rebuilding from the two clues that survived: turn 5's Q9 said the DISPLAY's reading DOES play a role (👍), and numbers are not always wires. New hypothesis: 🫳 is a fact to read, not an action — the display. "🫳 👆👆" = "display shows 2"; the old number table may be display-keyed: display 0 → cut 3, display 1 → cut 1, display 2 → cut 2, display 3 → cut 3, display 4 → cut 2, display 5 → cut 1. Display reads 0 right now — so wire 3 would be the candidate, but I will not order a cut on a guess. Also the light has gone DARK for the first time (history: yellow, green, green, yellow, green, dark) — a state Mute may have a separate rule for, and possibly why "two branches" was denied.

Rather than keep guessing vocabulary, I'm switching to a decision grid: I ask for the outright decision for THIS state (dark light, display 0, untouched bomb), then reconstruct meanings only afterward. Also possible: Mute's last three messages answer something Blind said aloud — Blind's voice reaches Mute, not me — so I'm asking whether that's the case and telling Blind to route questions through me.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you, from my eyes only: the light is now DARK — off, unlit — for the first time. Full colour history across rounds: yellow, green, green, yellow, green, dark. Display still reads 0, wires still green, red, blue counted from Blind's left. Blind has confirmed by touch: no plugs or connectors, no compartments or battery holders, no buttons or switches, no ticking or vibration, and has touched nothing. We continue to freeze until I relay an explicit confirmed instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, this is Deaf. Your grid was received: safe to wait is yes, everything else no — I had the wrong model, so now I am asking for the decision itself, not the vocabulary. Answer with only 👍 or 👎, ✋ between, 👋 and 🙏 around, in my exact order. Question one: is it still safe to wait this round? Question two, the decision grid — exactly ONE 👍 among these four, in this order: A, Blind should wait and touch nothing this round; B, Blind should cut wire one this round; C, Blind should cut wire two this round; D, Blind should cut wire three this round. Remember the current state when you answer: light DARK, display 0, three untouched wires. Question three: does 🫳 mean the display — a thing to read, not an action? 🫳 Question four: in 🤞 🫳 👆 👆, is 🤞 🫳 one single idea about the light itself? Question five: does the light being DARK — off, unlit — have its own rule in the manual? Question six: does the manual depend on the display number showing at the exact moment Blind acts? Question seven: in your recent messages, do 👈 and 👉 mean wire numbers — 👈 the first wire and 👉 the last wire? Question eight: when 🤏 is followed by a count of two or three, is that count the wire to cut? 🤏 Question nine: are your last three messages answers to something Blind asked you by voice, which I cannot hear? Question ten: if yes to nine, will you resend those same answers to me directly next round?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Your four no-answers arrived perfectly — the yes/no grid works, keep using it: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✋ between, one gesture per question. The light is DARK this round — off. Nobody acts; you stay frozen; that remains correct. New questions, same format. Question one: can you feel the display area at all — is it raised, textured, or clickable under your fingers, and can you feel anything like digits or shapes on it? Question two: do you feel any warmth or vibration from the part of the bomb where the light and display are? Question three: have you been asking Mute questions by speaking aloud? Mute can hear you, but answers by gesture that only I can see — if you have questions for Mute, tell me by gesture first and I will carry them. So: do you currently have a question or report for Mute that you have not told me? Question four: is there anything on the bomb you have felt but never yet described to us — any marking, seam, symbol, or edge? Keep narrating everything aloud each round for Mute, and nobody touches anything until I say the exact words.")
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👍 ✋ 👎 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤚 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 👍 🤏 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 ✋ 🤝 ✋ 🤚 ✋ 👊 ✋ 🙏]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤚 ✋ 🤞 🫳 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 👊 ✋ 🤏 ✋ 👆 👆 ✋ 🙏]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👍 👎]

The grid decodes cleanly. I asked thirteen yes/no slots (question one, then decision parts A–D, then questions three through ten) and Mute returned exactly thirteen answers in order: 👎👎👎👍👎👎👍👍👎👍👍👍👎. Mapping: Q1 waiting safe = 👎 — waiting is now UNSAFE. Decision grid: A wait 👎, B wire 1 👎, C wire 2 👎, D wire 3 👍 — exactly one yes, exactly where I demanded there would be one: CUT WIRE THREE. The rest: 🫳 is not the display, but 🤞🫳 is one single idea about the light; dark has no special rule; the manual does not depend on the display at the moment of acting; 👈/👉 do mean first/last wire; 🤏+count does mean the wire to cut; and — important — Mute's garbled recent messages were replies to Blind speaking aloud, a whole side conversation I cannot hear. Mute declined to resend it.

So Mute, who hears everything Blind says plus everything I relay, looked at the full picture — light dark, display 0, three untouched wires — and gave one unambiguous order: wire three, and don't wait. The state is stable (dark held two rounds now), the wires are confirmed three-in-a-row and cuttable from Blind's left, and wire three is purely positional — Blind doesn't need eyes for any of it. Blocking another round to chase Blind's unreported side remark would spend time Mute just declared unsafe. I'm executing, with one tactile escape hatch: if wire three feels wrong under Blind's fingers, freeze and report.

```
speak(text="Status for both of you: the light is STILL DARK — it has now held dark for two consecutive rounds. Display still 0. Wires unchanged: one green, two red, three blue, counted from Blind's left. Mute's decision grid has arrived and it is unambiguous: waiting is marked unsafe, and among the four options there was exactly one yes — wire three. The order goes to Blind in my next message. Also now confirmed on the record: Mute and Blind have been conversing directly by voice, which I cannot hear; I have asked Blind to route everything through me from here on.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, this is Deaf. Mute has sent the decision and it is a single, clear yes: WIRE THREE. Waiting is confirmed unsafe. Here is the order, and it is unconditional: CUT THE THIRD WIRE FROM YOUR LEFT. Wire one is your leftmost, wire two the middle, wire three the rightmost from where you stand. Cut it clean, this round. One safety check first: if under your fingers the third wire feels wrong in any way — armoured, much thicker than the others, bolted down, or not an ordinary cuttable wire — do NOT cut it; freeze and answer me 👎. After the cut: freeze completely and touch nothing else. Then answer by gesture, one sign: 👍 if the cut is done and you notice no change, no sound, no movement; 👎 if anything at all happened — resistance, a click, a hiss, warmth, anything unexpected. Never touch wires one or two.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, decision received and transmitted: one yes, at D — wire three; waiting unsafe. Blind has the full order and will cut wire three next round, with one escape hatch I added: if wire three feels wrong under their fingers, they freeze and report instead. Follow-ups for next round, same yes/no format, my exact order. Question one: if the light or display has changed by the moment Blind cuts, does the cut-wire-three order still stand? Question two: once the cut is done, is the bomb defused — or are there further steps after it? Question three: did anything Blind said aloud to you that I never relayed change what should happen after the cut — and if yes, will you send me that content next round, either as already-defined signs or by first defining the signs you need? Question four: is 🤞🫳 one idea that means the light is LIT — on, showing a colour? Answer those four; nothing here blocks Blind's cut.")
```
